summary: Initial integration discovery to evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for HelioForge's on-prem/edge inference needs. Key focus: gateway/proxy placement, SDK support (Golang + Python), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, rate limiting and quota controls, observability hooks, and a short benchmark pilot to validate latency/cost tradeoffs.
topics: Integration architecture; SDKs (Golang, Python), LangChain + LlamaIndex tooling; proxy/gateway vs sidecar; rate limits/quotas and token accounting; observability/tracing hooks; private deployment (VPC/on-prem) and key management; pilot next steps
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-27 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Liam (CTO HelioForge), Sofia (Platform Lead), Rajan (SRE), Mei (ML Eng)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick round-robin intros?
[00:07] Liam (HelioForge): Liam here, CTO. we're evaluating options for inference at our edge sites, have mix of cloud and colo. main asks are latency under 120ms p95 for short prompts and strict data residency.
[00:18] Sofia: hi, Sofia. handling platform infra, we'll own integration if we pull this forward.
[00:23] Rajan: Rajan, SRE. interested in quotas, rate limiting, and observability hooks.
[00:28] Mei: Mei, ML engine, working on prompt templates and LlamaIndex retrieval pipeline.
[00:34] Maya: great. i'll keep this high level and Ethan will jump in for architecture. main goals: confirm if Hosted can meet latency/cost, or if Dedicated/Private needed, and discuss gateway vs sidecar placement, SDKs, and LangChain/LlamaIndex patterns.
[00:49] Ethan (Redwood): quick context: Redwood supports Hosted API with regional routing, Dedicated GPU pools for guaranteed throughput, and Private deploy with VPC/on-prem. For edge we often see customers use a small proxy sidecar or a gateway adapter; both have tradeoffs.
[01:10] Liam: we tried a few hosted vendors, but token costs and privacy were concerns. can we get some clarity on where the data flows in Private vs Hosted?
[01:20] Maya: absolutely. Hosted => requests flow through our public control plane, models run in our managed infra; logs/usage are retained per tenancy but not in your VPC. Dedicated => reserved capacity in our cloud with customer-specific pools and stronger isolation; Private => control plane is customer-managed, deployments sit in your VPC or on-prem and logs stay inside. we'll send the runbook for exact network diagrams.
[01:46] Rajan: on the Private option, do we have to open inbound ports? firewall concerns.
[01:52] Ethan: most customers use outbound-only egress to our control plane and we pull model images from a registry. for air-gapped on-prem we support an appliance image. but yes, egress rules and registry access are required unless you do fully offline package. i'll include the checklist in the runbook.
[02:12] Mei: on the ML side — we use LlamaIndex for retrieval and LangChain around orchestration. do you have ready connectors or is it custom work?
[02:20] Ethan: we have SDKs for Python and Golang; LangChain and LlamaIndex community integrations exist and our SE team maintains example adapters. for some customers we provide a thin connector repo that maps LlamaIndex calls to our streaming chat/generation endpoints. sometimes the names in docs are off — folks call it Llama Index or LlamaIdx, so we've seen a mix.
[02:44] Mei: perfect, that's what i hoped. can we stream tokens back to the client and also do function/tool calling patterns?
[02:52] Ethan: yes, streaming is supported; function calling we map to structured JSON outputs and hooks. streaming includes interim tokens and we expose chunk boundaries for your runtime. sometimes the transcript shows 'K V cash' in old notes — that's our KV cache for context caching, reduces repeated tokens.
[03:12] Sofia: how do you recommend placing the proxy? our infra runs nginx gateway + envoy mesh. we prefer not to change the mesh config unless needed.
[03:22] Ethan: two common patterns: (1) edge gateway adapter — route requests from nginx/envoy through a lightweight proxy that handles batching, retry, and auth to Redwood; (2) sidecar per service that keeps KV cache local and handles prefix caching. gateway adapter is simpler for centralized control; sidecar gives lower tail latency because of local cache.
[03:41] Liam: tail latency is our big worry. 120ms p95 across global edges. can Hosted hit that?
[03:48] Maya: depends on sequence length and model. for small generation tasks (<=64 tokens) Hosted in nearby region can hit 120ms p95 for some optimized models; Dedicated with closer GPUs or Private on-prem will give tighter SLOs. we should run a benchmark with your workload.
[04:03] Rajan: about quotas/rate limits — we need token-level quotas per tenant and burst protection. how granular are your controls?
[04:11] Ethan: we offer per-token and per-request quotas via route-level policies. you can attach JWT scopes or API keys per tenant. burst capacity is managed by Dedicated pools with burst buckets or by a gateway that throttles. there is also a per-customer token accounting export for billing reconciliation.
[04:34] Rajan: do you expose proper headers for rate-limit remaining, reset, etc?
[04:39] Maya: yes, standard X-RateLimit style headers and webhook for quota events. also we have hooks into observability so you can identify hot routes.
[04:48] Mei: about embeddings and retrieval — we run an embeddings pipeline, store vectors in our Redis/FAISS. does Redwood provide embeddings or do we host ourselves?
[04:57] Ethan: both — you can call our embedding endpoints or host locally and use only generation in Redwood. some customers do embeddings locally for PII-sensitive data and call Redwood for generation only. index building patterns with LlamaIndex are straightforward, we have examples for FAISS, Milvus, Redis.
[05:15] Sofia: observability—what do you ship? tracing, token-level cost, per-request latency?
[05:21] Ethan: Redwood Console gives per-route token breakdown, latency percentiles, traces with OpenTelemetry spans, and payload sampling. For Private we can forward traces into your OTEL collector. there is also a tracing hook that adds a request_id and you can correlate with your logs.
[05:36] Liam: we need KMS integration for keys and HSM for certain customers.
[05:41] Maya: Private supports customer KMS/HSM via key wrapping and integration with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and on-prem HSM via PKCS#11. we'll include the KMS section in the runbook.
[05:53] Rajan: what about model provenance and model pinning? we want to freeze a model version for compliance.
[05:59] Ethan: model pinning is supported; you can pin a specific model digest. we keep model metadata and provenance in the catalog. also rollbacks and canary deployment are supported in Dedicated and Private.
[06:13] Mei: for LangChain usage, our code uses the Python llm wrapper. is there any custom code to swap in Redwood?
[06:20] Ethan: minimal. our Python SDK exposes a compatible API; we'll share example adapter code. LangChain and LlamaIndex need minor changes for streaming or function calling patterns. we'll send a working example that Mei can run locally.
[06:32] Sofia: security reviews — do you provide a penetration test report and third-party attestation?
[06:37] Maya: yes, SOC 2 Type II report, pen-test summary, compliance FAQ; for Dedicated/Private we can provide more detailed diagrams and network isolation proofs.
[06:48] Liam: pricing — baseline question: for Dedicated vs Hosted for our expected 2k requests/day with large bursts, what's the economics?
[06:58] Maya: Hosted is usage-based per token — good for low steady traffic and spikes; Dedicated has fixed monthly commit plus lower unit cost and more predictable latency. Private has license/engagement + infra costs. we'll produce a draft pricing sheet that maps to your traffic profile.
[07:15] Rajan: we plan to route traffic through our edge locations — want to avoid cross-region hops. is it possible to run a small private cluster in our colo that Redwood manages?
[07:25] Ethan: yes, we offer a Private on-prem option where the control plane is in your VPC and the inference runtime can be installed on your infra. there is also a lightweight appliance for colo. management can be via our operator or your team.
[07:36] Mei: one technical concern — KV cache coherence across sidecars. if we do sidecar per service how do you keep cache warm across nodes?
[07:44] Ethan: strategies: (1) local KV cache per sidecar with per-tenant TTL and warm-up on read; (2) shared prefix cache via Redis for cross-node sharing — tradeoff is added network hop. for best tail latency, prefer local caches and pre-warming during deployments.
[08:02] Sofia: can we do rate limiting at the gateway and still have Redwood do token accounting?
[08:08] Ethan: yes. the gateway can throttle at request level and pass along request metadata. Redwood can still do token accounting downstream; we accept batched requests and will return token usage per request in the response headers/payload so you can reconcile.
[08:23] Liam: are there known mis-transcriptions in docs? (laugh)
[08:27] Maya: (laugh) yes, sometimes our internal notes have "K V cash" or strange names.
[08:34] Mei: demo request — can Ethan show an example of a sidecar adapter code or a LangChain hook?
[08:39] Ethan: quick sketch: we have a python adapter that wraps the Redwood streaming client and implements the LangChain LLM interface; it handles chunked tokens and maps to LlamaIndex. i'll push an example to the repo and share link.
[08:54] Rajan: about quotas again — need emergency kill switch per tenant when PII leak suspected.
[08:59] Maya: we have suspend and revoke on API keys, and a rate-limit override that can zero-out capacity for a tenant. also alerting webhooks.
[09:09] Sofia: monitoring retention — logs/metrics retention window?
[09:13] Ethan: Hosted default is 90 days for metrics, logs 30 days; Dedicated can be configured longer, Private depends on your storage. we'll include retention options.
[09:25] Liam: integration timeline — if we start a pilot, how soon can we get an on-prem cluster up?
[09:30] Maya: pilot timeline typically 2-4 weeks: week 1 infra/network and runbook signoff, week 2 deploy small cluster and run bench, week 3 iterate on tuning and observability. full production depends on sizing and procurement.
[09:44] Mei: for the benchmark — we need to test: 1) p95 latency for 64-token completion, 2) cost per 1k tokens, 3) streaming reliability during bursts.
[09:55] Ethan: agreed. i'll include k6 and locust scripts and a small sample dataset. also will instrument OpenTelemetry spans so you can correlate latency hotspots.
[10:05] Rajan: are there limits on model sizes for on-prem? like 30B vs 70B differences?
[10:11] Ethan: hardware and quantization matter. 30B models are easier on smaller clusters; 70B needs more GPU memory or quantization to int8/4. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant and batching settings for your workload.
[10:25] Sofia: do you support autoscaling on Dedicated pools?
[10:29] Ethan: yes, Dedicated supports autoscale policies with burst capacity gates and cooldown; you can set SLOs to drive scale decisions.
[10:36] Liam: SLA?
[10:38] Maya: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets based on pool sizing. Private SLAs depend on the agreement.
[10:45] Mei: small detail — in the LangChain adapter, do you support function calling with tool result streaming?
[10:50] Ethan: we map function calls to structured JSON and can stream tool outputs as they arrive. sometimes LangChain expects a sync return; we added a shim for that in examples.
[10:59] Sofia: are there any gotchas for env proxies (we run mTLS inside mesh)?
[11:03] Ethan: mTLS is supported; the adapter authenticates to Redwood with short-lived tokens; in Private you can exchange mTLS certs for identity. we will include mTLS notes.
[11:14] Liam: cool. what's the easiest path to validate performance with minimal setup?
[11:18] Maya: two paths: Hosted quick smoke — call our Hosted endpoint from one edge node, run k6 for 24 hours. Or Private pilot — we deploy a tiny cluster in your colo, run the same k6 but with sidecar pattern. Hosted is fastest to start; Private gives representative tail latency.
[11:36] Rajan: cost of the Private pilot?
[11:39] Maya: pilot engagement has a small professional services fee to cover setup and support; we'll include numbers in the pricing doc.
[11:45] Mei: can you show the LangChain example to Mei and me in a follow-up?
[11:49] Ethan: yes, schedule a 60-min hands-on next week.
[11:53] Maya: okay quick recap of action items and next steps: Ethan will prepare benchmark plan and example adapters, Maya will send SOC2 + runbook + draft pricing, Liam will provide traffic profile. we'll aim to run benchmark week of Feb 8. Any final questions?
[12:10] Liam: all good, thanks.
[12:12] Sofia: thanks all.
[12:15] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and docs.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcript: natural filler and occasional mis-transcriptions present (e.g., KV cache rendered as K V cash in past notes). There were a few quick interruptions and cross-talks when scheduling follow-ups.
